question: Does a retained 12-input/3-output surjective routing admit cut-compatible tetrahedral realization, and is it the actual native proton C12-to-M3 transfer?
scope: Finite combinatorial routing and read-only exact source comparison. No native physical grading, charged sector, electron occupancy or assembled P/N/E dynamics is derived.
positive_candidate: The regular A4 action on twelve rotation labels, quotiented by its normal Klein-four subgroup, gives three four-element fibers.
tests_declared_before_checker_execution: Construct all twelve even permutations of four vertices and the Klein-four subgroup; verify group, normality, quotient and total/single-valued/surjective routing.
Exhaust all 5775 unlabeled balanced partitions of twelve inputs into three fours; determine which descend under the actual regular A4 relabelings.
Check left/right group cut relabelings; a swap within a fiber must descend, a swap of complete fibers must descend, but a single cross-fiber swap must not.
Retain the within-fiber label and reconstruct all twelve inputs; demonstrate that the three-output readout alone is not invertible.
Use unchanged actual proton geometry/rotation records if they form the advertised group, rather than identifying twelve ports with A4 solely by count.
Load exact native L/G/N operators with their original metric, derive their image encoders/decoders, and evaluate the actual C12-to-M3 forward map.

Report all output supports per native input, surjectivity, exact rank and any multiple-output witnesses. A rank-one map cannot be a weighted total single-valued surjection onto three independent output lines.
Do not replace the native transfer with the combinatorial quotient or discard native reader/history/complement data to force agreement.
classification_rule: The abstract candidate and its source identification receive separate verdicts. A valid abstract quotient does not accept the native or full-complex conjecture.
